listAcquisitions.sDispositionRationale: The remote client's OpenSSH launch, on the researcher's own host lane, outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8). It mutates nothing on this machine: it starts ssh, which opens a forward and runs a FIXED remote command. The argv is built by fsaBuildSshCommand from source text plus two validated values -- an int()-cast port and a destination that fnValidateSshDestination has matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$ and refused if it begins with a dash. The destination is its own argv element and never enters the remote command string, which matters because OpenSSH hands that string to the far side's LOGIN SHELL; this is also why the command carries no project name, a value that may legally contain a space. No shell=True, no user-supplied text in the command. Review relied on: fnValidateSshDestination, fiChooseLocalPort (port bounded 1..65535), fsaBuildSshCommand (the only argv builder), and tests/testRemoteClient.py, which pins the option-looking and shell-looking destinations as refusals and the absence of --project.

The remote helper's detached hub launch, on the researcher's own host lane, outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8: the hub itself is a trust judgement, not a capability the carrier grants). The argv is FIXED SOURCE TEXT in _fprocessStartDetachedHub -- sys.executable, -m vaibify, --no-browser, --port -- with the only interpolation an int()-cast port already bounded to 1..65535 by fnRemoteHelperCommand. No shell, no user string, and nothing from the SSH client reaches the argv: the client sends only a port, and fdictParseStartupRecord refuses a record naming any other one. The child is deliberately detached (start_new_session) because a closing laptop must not stop a running pipeline; it is therefore NOT journaled as a gated operation, because the journal keys by project and settles only on a dead holder with an empty process group, so a long-lived hub would leave a record that never settles and would permanently veto both the ownership reaper and idle shutdown. Review relied on: fnRemoteHelperCommand (port bound), _fnRefuseForeignListener and fdictFindCompatibleHub (a port already serving is refused, not adopted blindly), and the sessionRoutes _fprocessLaunchDetachedHub precedent this copies.

`vaibify sessions stop` on the researcher's own host lane, which is outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8: a trust judgement about the hub itself needs no capability). The PID comes from vaibify's own session registry and is checked for recycle-proof liveness before the signal; the signal is SIGTERM to a hub this user started.

A dynamic getattr over a THREE-ENTRY literal table of field names (_T_FIELD_DESCRIBERS), reading the config or wizard request for sContainerUser, sPythonVersion and sWorkspaceRoot. The names are source constants, never a request value, so no caller can reach an attribute the table does not list; the default is None, which the walk skips, so a partial object cannot raise. It reads only, and the values it reads are graded against literal format rules and returned as sentences (2026-09-21).

The build preflight measures the daemon's free disk by running df inside an image the daemon already holds: docker images -q, then docker run --rm --entrypoint df <id> -Pk /. Both launches are fixed argv lists with no shell; the one varying value is an image id the daemon itself reported, its own argv element, never a request field. Nothing is written and no container is touched -- the probe container is disposable and exits with df. Reachable from vaibify build and from the dashboard build route, where a disk the build cannot finish on is refused before a layer is written (2026-09-21, after a full daemon disk failed an overlay installer that blamed the network).

The build preflight asks each repository remote with git ls-remote --symref <url> HEAD refs/heads/<branch>: one fixed argv list, no shell, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 so a private remote fails rather than waits. The url and branch are vaibify.yml values already validated against the repository field character set and transport allow-list, each its own argv element. It reads the remote and writes nothing; no container is touched. Reachable from vaibify build, the dashboard build route and the setup wizard (2026-09-21, after a wizard-written main met a master remote).

The CPU worker pool (flistMapInWorkerProcesses). Its only caller is the transcript sanitizer's _flistSanitizePieces, which passes the fixed module-level function ftResultSanitizeText and argument tuples of already-fetched transcript text; the pool accepts no shell, command text or path. A worker imports vaibify's own code in a fresh interpreter as the hub's user, touches no container, Docker client, network or file, and writes nothing; results return to the parent, which lands them under the drain. Exact secrets travel over the pool's pipe, never argv or environment. The context is 'spawn' so no child inherits a lock from the multi-threaded hub, and the pool is bounded by os.cpu_count() - 1 and shut down before the call returns.

The one site that signals something vaibify did not create in this process: a host project's journaled process GROUP, on the researcher's own machine. Guarded three ways, each with a registered falsification -- the group is only ever one the host-exec journal recorded; it is signalled only while the holder pid is provably the recorded one (fbIsProcessAliveSince, recycle-proof), an unprovable identity being reported and routed to reconciliation rather than guessed at; and fbIsUsablePid refuses a zero or absent group id, which killpg would otherwise read as the CALLER's own group. Reached from POST /api/pipeline/{id}/kill under a mode-(b) carrier, and from `vaibify reconcile --terminate-recorded` on the host lane.

The environment-archive deposit's `docker save`, on the hub's own host lane. Two launches, both with a FIXED argv list and no shell: ['docker', 'save', sImageReference] in _fnStreamSaveIntoTarball and fsRecomputeImageStreamSha256. `docker save` mutates nothing -- it serializes an image out of the local store -- and the one value it carries is the image reference the project's own environment.json pins, read back from disk rather than taken from a request body. It is its own argv element, so it cannot become an option or a second command even if a hand-edited envelope spelled it that way; the worst a forged reference achieves is a non-zero exit, which the caller raises as CalledProcessError or reports as UNAVAILABLE. Review relied on: _fnStreamSaveIntoTarball, fsRecomputeImageStreamSha256 (the only two launch sites), fdictReadEnvironmentJson as the source of sImageReference, and tests/testEnvironmentArchive.py, which pins that an image the daemon cannot save reports UNAVAILABLE rather than a difference.

The local clone alone appends protocol.file.allow=always AFTER the hardening list, because a local path IS the file transport; it recurses into no submodule.
